hints: Focus on the polarity of the carbonyl group in ethanal and ask yourself which atom is electron poor and open to attack.
Remember KCN provides free cyanide ions, and the carbon end with its lone pair acts as the nucleophile in this reaction.
Check the curly arrows carefully, the arrow from the nucleophile must go to the carbonyl carbon while the C=O pi bond breaks onto oxygen.
walkthrough:
**Identify the electrophile in ethanal**

Think like a nucleophile looking for a positive spot. Oxygen is more electronegative than carbon, so the C=O bond is polarised as $\text{C}^{\delta+} - \text{O}^{\delta-}$.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{C}^{\delta+}(=\text{O}^{\delta-})\text{H}$$

**Identify the true nucleophile**

HCN is a weak acid and a poor nucleophile on its own. KCN provides $\text{CN}^-$ ions, and attack happens through the lone pair on carbon, written as $\text{:CN}^-$.

$$\text{KCN} \rightarrow \text{K}^+ + \text{:CN}^-$$

**Apply nucleophilic addition, first step**

The lone pair on $\text{:CN}^-$ forms a new C-C bond by attacking the $\delta+$ carbonyl carbon. At the same time the pi bond of C=O breaks, with both electrons moving onto oxygen to give an alkoxide intermediate.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CHO} + \text{:CN}^- \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{C}(\text{CN})(\text{O}^-)\text{H}$$

**Choose the correct curly arrow diagram**

The correct diagram must show two arrows: one from $\text{:CN}^-$ to the carbonyl C, and one from the C=O double bond up onto O. Only one option shows attack by the carbon end with both arrows in the correct direction.

options.A: Incorrect because the curly arrow is drawn backwards. The arrow is shown going from the C=O bond toward $\text{CN}^-$, which suggests electrons flowing to the nucleophile. In reality electrons flow from the nucleophile to the electrophile and from the C=O bond to oxygen.
options.B: Correct. It shows $\text{:CN}^-$ attacking the $\delta+$ carbonyl carbon with its carbon lone pair, while the C=O pi electrons move correctly onto the $\delta-$ oxygen to form the alkoxide intermediate $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}(\text{CN})\text{O}^-$. This is the accepted first step of cyanohydrin formation.
options.C: Incorrect because it shows attack through the wrong end of cyanide. The lone pair is drawn on nitrogen attacking carbon. The nucleophilic atom is carbon ($\text{:C}\equiv\text{N}$), not nitrogen, because C-C bond formation is required to make the hydroxynitrile product.
options.D: Incorrect because it shows $\text{H}^+$ attacking the carbonyl oxygen first. This is nucleophilic addition, not acid-catalysed electrophilic attack. The first step is attack by $\text{CN}^-$, protonation of the $\text{O}^-$ intermediate by HCN happens second.
